scores.reason: Measure type: insulin (with C-peptide and glucose) at nadir or during a mixed-meal test. Population: patients worked up for postprandial hypoglycaemia after bariatric surgery. Chain: US bariatric procedures 200,667 in 2024 (ASMBS 2026; 270,089 in 2023, ASMBS 2025) x medically attended post-bariatric hypoglycaemia 12% after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (29.4% of primary procedures, MBSAQIP 2024) and 5% after sleeve gastrectomy (70.6%) (PMID 41966914 Level A rates, abstract) = about 14,000 new medically attended cases a year (7,000-25,000); x evaluated with a glucose and insulin measurement during symptoms or a meal test about 60% (assumption, 30-90%) = about 8,500; plus retesting of the prevalent pool (160,000 requiring medical management per the same abstract) x about 5% a year (assumption, 2-10%) = about 8,000; x1.5 for work-ups that end negative (assumption, 1-2; clarification 4) = about 25,000 (range about 5,000-77,000). Incidence in the source ranges from 0.1% to 75% across studies by definition, which is why the range is wide.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR from fasting insulin and glucose). Population: adults with recent ischemic stroke or TIA without diabetes in whom the pioglitazone-by-IR decision arises (IRIS eligibility; ADA 2026 Rec 3.13 covers stroke with IR and prediabetes). Chain: ischemic stroke 692,000 a year (795,000 strokes x 87%, CDC) + TIA 240,000 (AHA 2023 statement, PMID 36655570; range 200,000-500,000) = about 930,000 (890,000-1.2 million); x without diabetes 70% (GWTG-Stroke: 29.6% had diabetes in patients aged 65 or older, PMID 29438515; range 65-80%) = about 650,000; x not excluded by heart failure, insulin treatment, age under 40, under 14 days after the event, death or severe disability about 70% (assumption, 50-85%) = about 455,000 (range 300,000-800,000). Bin 4 holds across the whole range. Narrower reading (also requiring IR, HOMA-IR above 3, about 25-40% of the pool; IRIS chose 3.0 as the top quartile in people without diabetes) gives about 140,000 (75,000-320,000): also bin 4, with the low end touching bin 3. Number of patients actually measured is far lower (not found; IRIS-style testing is not routine) but the clinical situation counts patients in whom the question arises.

anchor_issues: Row 6: the anchor 'patients in whom the clinical situation arises' and clarification 1 (share of existing pool evaluated in a year) give very different numbers (about 730,000 with unclear type versus about 37,000 evaluated). I followed clarification 1 and gave the broader number as a note. The bin therefore rests on an unsourced annual testing rate.
Row 5: clarification 4 (count everyone worked up) needs the number of negative work-ups, for which no source exists; I used a multiplier of 1.5 (range 1-2) as an assumption.

Row 13: clarification 2 (narrowest population) and clarification 4 point in opposite directions, because IR status is known only after the measurement. I took the pool eligible to be tested as the primary count and gave the IR-positive subset as a note; both fall in bin 4.

Rubric asks for at most 6 searches per row. Row 6 took more (11 PubMed strings, several returning 0 records, plus 4 web look-ups); the extra searches were mostly repeated attempts to find a US C-peptide testing rate or an insulin-treated pool count and found none. Logged in full in the report.
assumptions: Insulin-treated share of US adults with diagnosed diabetes about 25% (range 18-32%): no source was retrieved in this unit; CDC NDSR gives only the subsets (1.8 million with type 1 on insulin; 3.8 million who started insulin within a year of diagnosis).
Share of insulin-treated adults more than 3 years from diagnosis about 85% (unsourced).
Share with unclear or misclassified type about 12% (6-20%), anchored on 14% (UK, PMID 27080317) and 11% reclassified (Holt 2021); non-US and not specific to a US referral pattern.
Annual C-peptide evaluation rate among the unclear-type pool 5% (2-10%): no US source found; this is the bin-deciding share for row 6.

Row 5: share of medically attended post-bariatric hypoglycaemia that has a glucose and insulin measurement 60% (30-90%); retest rate of the prevalent pool 5% (2-10%); negative work-up multiplier 1.5 (1-2). Procedure volume held at the 2024 level of about 200,000; the 2023 level of 270,000 would raise the point estimate by about a third without changing the bin.

Row 13: 70% of ischemic stroke and TIA patients have no diabetes (GWTG-Stroke figure is for age 65 and older only); 70% pass exclusions (assumption); IR-positive share of 25-40% (assumption, IRIS threshold chosen as top quartile in non-diabetic populations). Stroke count includes recurrent strokes (185,000 a year); the TIA count is a 2002-based estimate.
Counts of strokes, TIAs and bariatric procedures are annual events or procedures, used as a proxy for patients; a person with two events in a year would be counted twice (small effect).
